source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)

verses.translation: And Yeshua [was] walking through Jericho.
verses.literal: And Yeshua [was] walking in Yericho.

verses.translation: And behold, a certain man came — his name [was] Zakkai — who was a chief [or: head, ruler] of the tax-collectors, and he was exceedingly [or: greatly] wealthy.

translation_notes: והנה (הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because the particle introduces a new character appearing on the scene, a classic use of the presentative 'behold'.

שר: Candidates: H8269 'a head person (of any rank or class)', H8270 'a string/umbilical cord'. Chose H8269 because in context this man holds authority over tax-collectors, making 'head person/chief' the coherent reading.

שהיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the ש prefix functions as a relative pronoun 'who' and היה as 'was', giving 'who was' — a natural description of the man's role.
textual_notes: העולמיים has no Strong's candidate provided. The consonants עולם typically mean 'eternity/world' (H5769), but in this context 'chief of the world-people' makes no sense. This appears to be a medieval Hebrew coinage for 'tax-collectors' or 'publicans' — possibly derived from a concept of worldly/fiscal affairs. The term is not standard biblical Hebrew and may reflect a later compositional layer.

verses.literal: And behold came a man one his name Zakkai who was chief [of] the tax-collectors and he was rich great.

verses.translation: And he was longing [or: desiring] greatly to see Yeshua the Anointed One — what sort of man he [was] — but he was not able to see him on account of the multitude of the people, for that Zakkai was small [or: short] of stature [or: form].

translation_notes: חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline to/be pleased/desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/valuable thing'. Chose H2654 as the verbal form because the sentence structure (והיה חפץ) indicates an active state of desiring, not a noun.

משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'contemplation/utterance', H7880 'a shoot/shrubbery'. Chose H4899 because it follows the proper name Yeshua as a title — 'Yeshua the Anointed One' is the natural reading.

אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'howler/wild creature', H339 'habitable spot/island'. Chose H335 as an interrogative 'which/what kind of' because the phrase 'אי זה איש הוא' reads as an embedded question: 'what sort of man he was.'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה together form the interrogative 'which/what kind of', a known Hebrew construction.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/self/the same', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun completing the embedded question 'what man he [was].'
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5973 'with/among'. Chose H5971 because 'the people' is the coherent object after 'multitude of' — referring to the crowd.
textual_notes: The consonants ק טן appear to be a single word קטן (H6996, 'small/young/insignificant') split across a word boundary, possibly due to scribal practice or manuscript damage. Reading them together as קטן makes full sense: 'small of form/stature.'
הצורה (H6699) means 'form' or 'figure' — here it functions as 'stature/physical form,' describing Zakkai's short physical build.
אותו could be parsed as the accusative marker + 3ms suffix ('him') or as a demonstrative. In context it seems to function as a connector: 'for that [same] Zakkai was small of stature.'

verses.literal: And he was desiring very much to see Yeshua [the] Anointed One which this man he [was] and not [he] was able to see him on account of [the] multitude [of] the people for that Zakkai was small [of] the form.

verses.translation: And he ran and climbed up into a certain tree — its name [was] sycamore — in order that he might be able to see Yeshua the Anointed One, for there he was [about] to pass by.

translation_notes: ועלה: Candidates: H5927 'to ascend/mount', H5928 'a holocaust', H5929 'a leaf', H5930 'a step/holocaust', H5931 'a pretext'. Chose H5927 because the narrative describes physical action — running and then climbing up into a tree.

שקמה: Candidates: H8256 'a sycamore (tree)', H7054 'something that rises/stalk of grain'. Chose H8256 because the context identifies it as the name of the type of tree (אילן) he climbed — a sycamore tree fits perfectly.

שם: Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem'. Chose H8033 'there' because the sentence describes the location where Yeshua was about to pass — 'for there he was to pass.'

יוכל: The only Strong's candidate is H3116 'Jukal, an Israelite' (a proper name). However, the consonants י-כ-ל clearly represent the imperfect form of יכל 'to be able' (from the root כול/יכל). In context 'in order that he would be able to see' is the only coherent reading. The Strong's number for the verb 'to be able' is H3201.

לעבור: Candidates: H5668 'transit/on account of', H5669 'stored grain'. The root עבר (H5674) means 'to pass over/through.' Here the infinitive לעבור means 'to pass by,' describing Yeshua's anticipated route.
textual_notes: ורץ is listed only under H7518 'a fragment', but the consonants רץ also represent the participle or past form of רוץ (H7323, 'to run'). In context, 'he ran' is the only coherent reading. The narrative describes physical urgency: running ahead and climbing a tree.

יוכל: The Strong's candidate H3116 is a proper name 'Jukal'. In this context it must be the imperfect of יכל 'to be able' (H3201). The consonants are identical but the narrative demands the verbal reading.

verses.literal: And he ran and went up in a tree one its name sycamore in order that he would be able to see Yeshua [the] Anointed One for there he was to him to pass.

verses.translation: And when Yeshua came to the place, [he] looked up and saw Zakkai, and Yeshua the Anointed One said to him: Zakkai, come down quickly and make haste, for I am compelled [or: it is necessary for me] to come today into your house.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when/where', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר is a standard temporal conjunction meaning 'when/as' — introducing the moment Yeshua arrived at the spot.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'near/to/among'. Chose H413 because 'came to the place' is the natural directional reading.
המקום: Candidates: H4725 'a standing/place/locality', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because the narrative describes Yeshua arriving at a specific location — 'the place' where Zakkai was in the tree.
וראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'a vulture', H7203 'a seer/vision'. Chose H7200 because the verb 'and he saw' continues the narrative action of looking up and perceiving.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context introduces direct speech — 'and said to him.'

מהר: Candidates: H4116 'to hurry', H4117 'to bargain for a wife', H4118 'in a hurry', H4119 'a price for a wife', H2022 'a mountain'. Chose H4116/H4118 because the command 'come down quickly' demands urgency, not marriage or mountains.

וחושה: The only candidate is H2364 'Chushah, an Israelite (proper name)'. However, the consonants חוש represent the root חוש (H2363, 'to hurry/hasten'). The ה suffix is the cohortative/imperative ending. In context, 'and hurry!' is the only coherent reading paired with 'come down quickly.'
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'compelled am I' requires the first person pronoun.
textual_notes: The subject of הביט and וראה is ambiguous. The text reads 'Zakkai looked up and saw Yeshua the Anointed One' — but it could also be parsed as 'Yeshua looked up and saw Zakkai.' The word order (ישוע בא אל המקום ... הביט וראה) could attach the verbs to either party. However, the phrase order suggests Yeshua came to the place, then [he] looked up — since Zakkai was above in the tree, looking 'up' more naturally describes the one on the ground (Yeshua) looking upward. But the traditional narrative has Yeshua looking up at Zakkai. Either parsing is syntactically possible.

מוכרח has no Strong's candidate provided. The root כרח implies compulsion/necessity. This appears to be a later Hebrew formation (hophal/pual participle of כרח) meaning 'compelled/necessitated.' It is not standard biblical Hebrew vocabulary.
וחושה: H2364 is a proper name, but the consonants clearly function here as an imperative of חוש 'to hurry.' The Strong's number for the verbal root would be H2363.

verses.literal: And when Yeshua came to the place Zakkai looked up and saw Yeshua [the] Anointed One and said to him Zakkai come down quickly and hurry for compelled [am] I that I will come today in your house.

verses.translation: And Zakkai descended quickly and received Yeshua in joy.

translation_notes: ירד: Candidates: H3381 'to descend/go down', H3382 'Jered (name)'. Zakkai was up in a tree and was told to come down — 'descended' is the clear reading. Chose H3381.
מהרה: Candidates: H4120 'a hurry/promptly', H2029 'to become pregnant', H2030 'pregnant'. As an adverb describing the speed of descent, 'quickly' is obvious. Chose H4120.

וקבל: Candidates: H6901 'to admit/take/receive', H6902 'to acquire', H6903 'in front of/on account of', H6904 'battering-ram', H6905 'presence/in front of'. Describing welcoming a guest, 'received/welcomed' fits perfectly. Chose H6901.
בשמחה: Candidates: H8057 'blithesomeness/glee/joy', H4229 'to stroke/erase'. With ב prefix meaning 'with/in,' the reading 'with joy' is the natural one. Chose H8057.

verses.literal: And Zakkai descended quickly and received Yeshua in joy.

verses.translation: And when the people that saw this they murmured all of them in their midst saying that in [the] house of a man sinning he entered.

translation_notes: וכאשר: כאשר = 'when/as' (H834 as conjunction). Chose H834.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/crowd', H5972 same, H5973 'with', H5974 'with'. Subject of the verb 'saw' — 'the people.' Chose H5971.
ההוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/that', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. As a demonstrative modifying העם — 'that people/those people.' Chose H1931.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. As main verb 'saw,' chose H7200.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Object of seeing — 'this [thing].' Chose H2088.
שבבית: ש (that/in) + ב (in) + בית. Candidates for בית: H1004 'house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith (place)'. 'In the house of' — chose H1004.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'turn rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Describing the householder as a sinner — 'a man/person.' Chose H120.
textual_notes: התלוננו — hitpolel perfect of לון/לין (to murmur/grumble, H3885), 3mp + 'they murmured.' This is a post-biblical form but clearly contextual.
כולם — כל (all, H3605) + suffix הם (them) = 'all of them.'
בקרבם — ב + קרב (midst, H7130) + suffix הם = 'in their midst/among themselves.'
חוטא — qal participle of חטא (to sin, H2398) = 'sinning/a sinner.'
נכנס — niphal perfect of כנס (to gather/enter) — a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'he entered.' Not in classical biblical Hebrew Strong's.

verses.literal: And when the people that saw this they murmured all of them in their midst saying that in [the] house of a man sinning he entered.

verses.translation: And Zakkai standing said to Yeshua: Lord, I [am] desiring to give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have defrauded any man, I [am] desiring to return to him the thing that in four-fold.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. As main verb of speech, chose H559.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord/controller', H114 'Addon (name)'. As a form of address to Yeshua, 'Lord/Master' is the clear reading. Chose H113.
אני (both): H589 'I' or H590 'ship/fleet'. First person pronoun in self-referential speech. Chose H589.
חפץ (both): Candidates: H2654 'to desire/be pleased with', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/matter'. As a verb expressing intention ('I desire to give/restore'), chose H2654.
חצי: Candidates: H2677 'the half/middle', H2678 'an arrow'. Before 'my possessions,' 'half' is the coherent reading. Chose H2677.
ואם: H517 'mother' or H518 'if/although'. Introducing a conditional clause ('and if I defrauded'), chose H518.
שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/set (any)', H7761 same, H7762 'garlic'. Before אדם ('person'), שום functions as 'any' — a Mishnaic usage meaning 'any/some.' Chose H7760 for the functional range.
אדם: H120 'a human being.' Object of defrauding — 'any person.' Chose H120.
הדבר: Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1697 'a word/matter/thing'. With article ה, 'the thing/matter' that was taken. Chose H1697.
ההוא: H1931 'he/that.' Demonstrative modifying הדבר — 'that thing.' Chose H1931.

להשיב: The candidates given (H7867-7869) relate to aging/growing gray, but להשיב is clearly the hiphil infinitive of שוב (H7725, to return/restore). 'To restore/give back' is the obvious meaning in context of restitution.
textual_notes: עומד — qal participle of עמד (to stand, H5975). 'Standing' — no candidates provided but form is standard.
לתת — infinitive construct of נתן (to give, H5414) with ל prefix. Standard form.
נכסי — נכסים (possessions/property) + suffix י (my). This is a post-biblical Hebrew/Aramaic term (related to H5233 נכס). 'My possessions.'
לעניים — ל + עניים (poor ones), plural of עני (H6041, poor/afflicted). 'To the poor.'
רימיתי — appears to be a piel perfect 1cs of רמה (H7411, to deceive/defraud) = 'I have defrauded/cheated.' The spelling with י is a later Hebrew orthographic convention.
בארבעה — ב + ארבעה (four, H702). 'In four [measures].'
כפלים — plural/dual of כפל (H3718, double/fold). 'Folds/doublings.' Combined with בארבעה: 'fourfold.'

verses.literal: And Zakkai standing said to Yeshua: Lord, I [am] desiring to give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have defrauded any man, I [am] desiring to return to him the thing that in four-fold.

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to him: today [was] made peace in this the house on account of that this [is] a son of Abraham.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say.' Speech verb. Chose H559.
היום: H3117 'a day/today' or H3118 'a day'. With article, 'today.' Chose H3117.

שלום: Candidates: H7965 'safe/well/peace/welfare/prosperity', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. After 'was made,' 'peace/salvation/wholeness' produces the most meaningful image. Chose H7965.

בזה: Candidates: H959 'to despise', H960 'scorned', H961 'booty', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Parsing as ב (in) + זה (this) = 'in this.' A preposition + demonstrative before הבית ('the house') is natural. Chose H2088 for זה.
הבית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'object marker'. With article, 'the house.' Chose H1004.
בעבור: H5668 'on account of/because' or H5669 'stored grain'. Introducing causal clause. Chose H5668.
שזה: ש (that/because) + זה. H2088 'this.' 'Because this [one]...' Chose H2088.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son'. Describing lineage — 'a son of Abraham.' Chose H1121.
textual_notes: נעשה — niphal perfect of עשה (to do/make, H6213) = 'was made/has been made.' Standard form.
שלום could carry its full semantic range here: peace, wholeness, salvation, well-being. The Hebrew concept is broader than any single English word.
The word בזה could theoretically be parsed as the verb 'to despise' (H959), but in context before הבית it clearly functions as preposition + demonstrative.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said to him: today [was] made peace in this the house on account of that this [is] a son of Abraham.

verses.translation: Came to seek [the] son of the man to save what was lost.

translation_notes: לבקש: Candidates: H1245 'to search out/seek/strive after', H7179 'straw'. The infinitive 'to seek' after 'came' is the clear reading — purpose of coming. Chose H1245.
בן: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben', H1123 'a son'. In the phrase 'son of the man/human,' this is a well-known Hebraic title. Chose H1121.
האדם: Candidates: H119 'turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. With the article ה, 'the human/the man' — forming the title 'Son of Man.' Chose H120.
מה: H4100 'what?/that which' or H4101 same. As a relative pronoun 'what/that which [was lost],' chose H4100.
textual_notes: The word order is unusual: 'came to seek son of the man to save what was lost.' It could be parsed as 'the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost' — where בן האדם is the subject and בא is the main verb. The word order (verb first, then purpose infinitives, then subject) is possible in Hebrew but awkward; alternatively בן האדם could be the object of לבקש ('came to seek the Son of Man, to save what was lost'), though the former reading is more natural given the broader narrative.
<היה — the < symbol appears to be a manuscript mark or damage. Reading as שהיה or simply היה (was, H1961). Combined with אבוד, it means 'was lost.'
אבוד — passive participle of אבד (to perish/be lost, H6). 'Lost/perishing.' No candidates were provided.
להושיע — hiphil infinitive of ישע (to save/deliver, H3467) with ל prefix. 'To save.' The root relates to the name ישוע itself.

verses.literal: Came to seek [the] son of the man to save what was lost.

verses.translation: And this he said to those the men on account of that he was [a] prophet to Jerusalem and because they thought that immediately would be revealed [the] kingdom [of] heaven

translation_notes: וזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'and this' fits naturally as introducing what he said.
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context requires a verb of speech — 'he said.'
שהיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because 'that he was a prophet' is coherent; 'ruin' makes no sense here.
שמים (consonants שמים): Candidates: H8064 'sky/heaven', H4325 'water', H3220 'sea'. Chose H8064 because 'kingdom of heaven' is a coherent phrase in this context about prophetic expectation.

שמיד: The ש is the relative particle 'that', and מיד means 'from hand' i.e. 'immediately/at once' (from H3027 יד 'hand' with prefix מ). Chose this reading because the sentence speaks about their expectation of an imminent revelation.
textual_notes: שמיד is parsed as ש + מיד ('that immediately'). The word מיד derives from יד (H3027 'hand') with the prepositional prefix מ, yielding the adverbial sense 'from the hand' = 'immediately.' This is a common Hebrew idiom but not explicitly listed as a separate Strong's entry.

verses.literal: And this he said to those the men on account of that he was [a] prophet to Jerusalem and because they thought that immediately would be revealed [the] kingdom [of] heaven

verses.translation: And then he said [a] man one noble went to [a] kingdom one very far in order that he would take [a] kingdom for himself and that he would return

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'a man/person' fits the parable context of introducing a character.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one man' = 'a certain man' is natural narrative introduction.
הלך (consonants הלך): Candidates: H1980 'to walk/go', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'a journey', H1983 'toll'. Chose H1980 because the context requires a verb of motion — 'he went.'
מאד (consonants מאד): Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/very', H108 'fog'. Chose H3966 because 'very far' is the natural adverbial modifier for רחוק.
בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because the purpose clause 'in order to receive kingship' fits the narrative.
textual_notes: מעולה has no Strong's candidates provided. It appears to be a passive participle from עלה ('to go up'), meaning 'exalted, noble, of high rank.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew form.
ושיחזור has no Strong's candidates. It is ו + ש + יחזור (and + that + he would return), from חזר 'to return,' a common post-biblical Hebrew verb not represented in the Strong's lexicon.

verses.literal: And then he said [a] man one noble went to [a] kingdom one very far in order that he would take [a] kingdom for himself and that he would return

verses.translation: And he called ten servants his and he gave to them ten minas and he said to them do your expenditures from these the minas until that I come

translation_notes: וקרא (consonants קרא): Candidates: H7121 'to call out/summon', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 because summoning servants fits the narrative action perfectly.

שלו (consonants שלו): Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'a fault', H7961 'tranquil/careless'. In context, שלו functions as the possessive pronoun 'his' (ש + לו = 'that [belong] to him'). None of the Strong's entries apply directly; this is a syntactic construction rather than a lexical entry.
ונתן (consonants נתן): Candidates: H5414 'to give', H5415 'give', H5416 'Nathan'. Chose H5414 because the verb 'gave' fits the action of distributing money.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 as the 3rd person plural pronoun 'to them' with the preposition ל.
עשר (consonants עשר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth'. Chose H6235 because 'ten minas' matches 'ten servants' in the parable.

עשו: The only Strong's candidate is H6215 'Esau.' However, in context this is clearly the imperative plural of עשה 'to do/make' — a basic verb form not matched to the proper noun. The consonants עשו serve as the command 'do/make.'
עד (consonants עד): Candidates: H5703 'duration', H5704 'until/as far as', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 because 'until I come' is the temporal clause.
textual_notes: עשו could consonantally match H6215 'Esau,' but context demands the imperative plural of עשה 'to do/make.' No Strong's entry for the verb עשה was listed among the candidates.
שלו is parsed as ש + לו ('that [belong] to him' = 'his'), a common relative possessive construction in post-biblical Hebrew, rather than any of the lexical entries provided.
מנים (no candidates provided) — parsed as plural of מנה (mina, H4488), a unit of weight/currency.
הוצאותיכם (no candidates provided) — plural noun with 2mp suffix, from יצא in the causative, meaning 'your expenditures' or 'your business dealings.'

verses.literal: And he called ten servants his and he gave to them ten minas and he said to them do your expenditures from these the minas until that I come

verses.translation: And they angered him — his citizens already — and they sent [messengers] after him saying not we desire that this one should reign over us

translation_notes: כבר (consonants כבר): Candidates: H3527 'to augment/multiply', H3528 'long ago/formerly/already', H3529 'Kebar river'. Chose H3528 because 'already' fits temporally — the citizens had already been hostile.
שזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'that this one should reign' is the coherent protest of the citizens.
לא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not'. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: ע appears to be a truncated or abbreviated form. It may be a scribal abbreviation or a fragment of a longer word. Possibly עם ('with') or the abbreviation of a word. The text may be corrupt at this point.

ירוניו has no candidates provided. It appears to be a plural noun with 3ms suffix, possibly from עיר ('city') yielding 'his city-dwellers/citizens,' though the consonantal form is unusual — perhaps a variant of עירוניו.

והקציפוהו has no candidates. It parses as a Hiphil perfect 3cp of קצף ('to be angry') with 3ms object suffix — 'they made him angry' or 'they angered him.' Alternatively it could mean 'they were angry at him.'
The bracket around מלאכים in the source text suggests it may be a scribal insertion or gloss.

verses.literal: And they angered him — his citizens already — and they sent [messengers] after him saying not we desire that this one should reign over us

verses.translation: And it was done when he returned from the kingdom he commanded that they would call to him the servants those that he gave to them the money in order that he would know how much spent each one and one

translation_notes: כאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר = 'when/as' — a temporal conjunction introducing the return.

אתה (ʾTH): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 (Aramaic 'arrive'), H859 'you'. Chose H859 'you' — addressing someone directly before the verbs that follow.

הכרת (HKRT): H3772 'to cut off'. But as discussed in section 2, the consonants also match hifil of נכר (H5234) 'to recognize/discern'. Here the sentence seems to address 'you' with two perfect verbs. 'You have recognized' makes sense as a declaration.

הרדכת: Not fully listed. Consonants HRDKhT suggest hifil perfect 2fs/2ms of רדך or a form of ירד (H3381) 'to go down' in a causative/intensive form, or רדד (H7286) 'to beat down/subdue/spread'. Reading as 'you have submitted/been brought low' from רדד or a related root.
textual_notes: The final clause 'ואמר אתה הכרת הרדכת' is highly ambiguous. It could be: (a) 'And he said: You have recognized, you have submitted'; (b) 'And it was said: You have been cut off, you have been trampled'; (c) A separate speaker or editorial note.

הכרת could be from כרת H3772 'to cut off' (hifil 2ms perfect) or from נכר H5234 'to recognize' (hifil 2ms perfect). Both are consonantally valid. In isolation 'you have recognized' pairs strangely with 'you have submitted', but both could be addressing the city/people about their fate.

הרדכת is obscure. Possible roots: רדך (unattested as standard), ירד H3381 'to descend' in some derived form, or רדד H7286 'to beat down/subdue'. The ד-כ combination is unusual. This may be a hapax or dialectal form. If from רדד + כ insertion, it could mean 'you have been beaten down/subdued'.
שומעין and מקשיבין both use -ין endings (Aramaic-style plurals), confirming the late linguistic register of this text.
The transition from the narrative third person to direct speech ('and he said: you...') is abrupt; it is unclear whether this concludes the passage or begins a new speech unit.

verses.literal: And not they found what to do to him because all the people [were] listening to him attending to him and he said you have recognized you have submitted
